newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya says air embargo over after balloon flew by.
newsitem.headline: Libya says air embargo over after balloon flew by.

text.p: Libya says the U.N. flight embargo has been lifted now that an American balloonist flew over part of the country after getting belated permission from Tripoli.

The official Libyan news agency JANA said on Saturday the foreign ministry sent the U.N. Security Council a letter explaining that due to the embargo Libya originally denied Steve Fossett permission but the change meant planes could also fly in and out of the country.

"Accordingly we in Libya hereby grant permission as of this moment to the balloon to cross Libyan airspace and accept the crossing by any foreign aircraft of Libyan airspace and landing at its airports," the ministry said.
"Furthermore, Libyan Arab airliners will immediately resume their flights to other countries," the agency, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, quoted the ministry as saying.

Fossett, who is trying to make the first nonstop global balloon flight, was forced to detour on Friday when he could not get permission from Libya to enter its airspace. When the permission came through late on Friday he altered course, but the change cost him heavily in speed and fuel.
The embargo was slapped on Libya for refusing to turn over to the United States or Britain two suspects in the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am airliner, in which 270 people were killed.
